references.text: God's original instructions to Moses to build the incense altar of acacia wood, with the same dimensions: one cubit long, one cubit wide, square, and two cubits high, with horns that were part of the altar.
The ark of the covenant was also made of acacia wood (עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים), the same material as the incense altar.
The bronze altar for burnt offerings was also made of acacia wood and had horns at its four corners, similar to the incense altar.
Solomon's temple also contained an incense altar of cedar overlaid with gold, serving as a replacement for the tabernacle's incense altar.
King Uzziah unlawfully attempted to burn incense on the incense altar in the temple, demonstrating the altar's holiness.
Zechariah was serving at the incense altar in the temple when the angel Gabriel appeared to him.
The book of Hebrews mentions the golden incense altar as part of the sacred furnishings of the tabernacle.
Revelation describes incense rising from the golden altar before God's throne, symbolizing the prayers of the saints.
Direct correspondence between God's instructions (Ex 30:2) and their actual execution (Ex 37:25), confirming faithfulness to the task.
